claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Aluminizing cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a thin protective Al2O3 scale.
The proposed pack-cementation or vapor-deposition treatment will deposit a uniform aluminum surface layer.
Controlled heat treatment after aluminum deposition will develop a compact, adherent Al2O3 scale.
Aluminum enriched at the alloy surface will selectively oxidize during high-temperature exposure.
Selective oxidation of surface aluminum will produce a stable Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into the alloy bulk.
Restricting oxygen diffusion will reduce harmful internal oxidation.
The aluminized alloy will have markedly lower oxygen uptake than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure at about 1000 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere for about 100 hours.
The aluminized alloy will show minimal internal oxidation relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminizing will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility within 8–16%.
Aluminizing will preserve yield strength within 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes significant oxygen penetration and oxidation under comparable high-temperature exposure.
The intervention is expected to remain effective around 1000 °C in oxidizing atmospheres for exposure durations on the order of 100 hours and under low-strain-rate mechanical testing.
